dedupe_keys.name: openconfig vendor neutral yang data models and gnmi telemetry for network device management

description: OpenConfig publishes vendor-neutral data models for configuring and monitoring network devices, together with the gRPC-based management and streaming telemetry protocols that use them. It is an open-source project led by an Operator Working Group of network operators, with contributions from equipment vendors. Coverage: generic models used by operators worldwide for routers, switches, optical transport and wireless access points, covering interfaces, routing protocols such as BGP and IS-IS, MPLS, QoS, platform components, optical amplifiers and terminal devices, and access points. Format and access: YANG 1.0 modules in the openconfig/public GitHub repository with generated schema documentation on the website, and protocol specifications (gNMI, gNOI, gRIBI) with reference code; free. Licence: Apache 2.0. Caveats: the models describe what a device can report and accept, not any operator's network, so they are a schema for inventories and telemetry, not data; vendor support for each model path varies. Simulation uses: a common schema for building network topology and state inputs to digital twin and capacity planning models of telecom networks, and for streaming telemetry into them. Related records: the YANG module collection (data-yangmodels-yang-module-collection) gathers IETF, IEEE and vendor models alongside, the TM Forum Information Framework (data-tm-forum-information-framework-sid) models the operator business layer, and Containerlab (platform-containerlab) runs device labs driven by such models.
